title: DynArray — Your Own Vector
hints: Doubling the capacity is what makes `push_back` cheap on average: most calls just write into space that is already there.
`insert(index, value)` makes room first, then moves every element from the end down to `index` one place right, starting from the end so nothing is overwritten. `erase` moves them one place left.
requirements: Extends `IntArray` from [[7.08 Container Classes and initializer_list]] with **capacity** and amortized growth
`at()` with bounds checking (print an error for now)
stretch: Shrink-to-fit, and a benchmark against `std::vector<int>` for a million `push_back`s.
